answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited stake registry: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can post offers, and slashing removes stake when it double-claims work or breaks a verified contract. A trellis of signed, auditable task links lets peers detect reused claims; a walnut-sized deposit is not enough if repeated participation requires more capital. The prism is that Sybils can still appear, but matching their honest agents’ influence forces the attacker to buy and risk stake, not merely mint identities.
